hook: Ali Ghodsi was born in Tehran, Iran, and grew up in Sweden, studying at the KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Mid Sweden University before doing postdoctoral research at UC Berkeley's AMPLab. There he co-created Apache Mesos, a system for sharing compute resources across a data center cluster, and worked alongside the researchers who built Apache Spark. In 2013 he co-founded Databricks with that same group to commercialize Spark as a managed data platform. As CEO, he has pushed Databricks toward what the company calls a lakehouse architecture, combining the flexibility of data lakes with the reliability of data warehouses, and has driven the platform's expansion into machine learning and generative AI workflows. He remains an adjunct faculty member in UC Berkeley's EECS department.
